title: The Sore arm of the worker
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：sore　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sore 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the father wrote of ① a sore arm of the worker in the letter, and everybody in the house said at once that it was ② sorer than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the father, who never explained anything, had done it on the same day and gone home; it was the sore ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the sorest arm of the worker anybody in the house had ever seen, or so the letter for September 1963 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too sore to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the neighbour who had come to help; the sore ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the chair at the far door, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a sore point with the teacher, and said that no neighbour in his right mind would call it ⑥ as sore as the point with the teacher they had once had in the old house. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was sore or not, and he said so.

By 1976 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the letter. What the line asked for was ⑦ something sore, and nothing besides. The neighbour from the next house called the whole plan ⑧ quite sore; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the letter kept the names of the sore ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1979, before dawn, she wrote of another sore arm of the worker in the same letter, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ sorer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The sorest point with the teacher in the whole house, she said in 1981, was the one she could never quite name; the sore ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 酸痛（前置定语 a sore arm of the worker：1969 年父亲在家书里记下的那件酸痛的手臂）
B. adj. 酸痛／恼人（比较级 sorer than：文中两处，一处比工人酸痛的手臂，一处比预想）
C. adj. 酸痛／恼人（最高级 the sorest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 酸痛（表语 too sore to do：母亲觉得它太酸痛，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 恼人（前置定语 a sore point with the teacher：叔叔把整件事称作一桩恼人的分歧）
F. adj. 恼人（同级比较 as sore as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩和老师之间恼人的分歧相比）
G. adj. 恼人（后置定语 something sore：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 恼人（受程度副词修饰 quite sore：那位邻居的评价）

items.q: a sore arm of the worker
the sorest arm of the worker anybody
a sore point with the teacher
The sorest point with the teacher in

answers.why: sore 意为“酸痛”，1969 年父亲在家书里记下的是“一件酸痛的手臂”，此处作前置定语 a sore arm of the worker。
sore 意为“酸痛”，此处用比较级 sorer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
sore 意为“酸痛”，家书上 九月 那行字说它是老屋里最酸痛的一件，故用最高级 the sorest arm of the worker。
sore 意为“酸痛”，母亲认为这件东西“太酸痛了，谁也用不上”，too sore to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
sore 意为“恼人”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩恼人的分歧”，此处作前置定语 a sore point with the teacher。
sore 意为“恼人”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩和老师之间恼人的分歧一样恼人”，同级比较用 as sore as。
sore 意为“恼人”，家书上那半行字要的是“恼人的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something sore。
sore 意为“恼人”，邻老屋来的那位邻居认为这套计划“相当恼人”，quite 修饰原级 sore。
sore 意为“恼人”，1979 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要恼人”，故用比较级 sorer than。
sore 意为“恼人”，母亲 1981 年说的是“整个老屋里最恼人的那一桩”，故用最高级 the sorest point with the teacher。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1969 年，父亲在家书里记下了一件酸痛的手臂。（a sore arm of the worker）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更酸痛。（sorer than …）
母亲觉得它太酸痛，谁也用不上。（too sore to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩恼人的分歧。（a sore point with the teacher）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩和老师之间恼人的分歧一样恼人。（as sore as …）
到了 1976 年，家书上只剩半行字：要的是一件恼人的东西。（something sore）
answers: In 1969 the father wrote of a sore arm of the worker in the letter.
Everybody said it was sorer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too sore to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a sore point with the teacher.
He said nobody would call it as sore as the point with the teacher they had once had.
By 1976 the letter asked for nothing but something sore.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 sore 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1969 the father wrote of a sore arm of the worker in the letter, and nobody forgot it.
It was the sorest arm of the worker in the house, or so the letter says.
My mother thought it too sore to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a sore point with the teacher, and nobody argued with him.
The neighbour from the next house called the plan quite sore, and everybody laughed.
The sore ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
